In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of quasi-exactly-solvable potentials with known zero energy solutions.
the construction of quasi-exactly soluble models with known zero-energy states.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zero-energy states of quasi-exactly-solvable rational potentials are not normalizable and, consequently, they do not represent bound states of the corresponding quantum mechanical problem.
the zero-energy solutions of quasi-exactly soluble rational potentials are not normalizable and do not describe bound states.
the zero-energy states are bound states for a large class of quasi-exact solvable potentials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quasi-exactly solvability is a property of the zero-energy states of the potential algebra.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of zero-energy bound states for a rational potential is not a sufficient condition for its integrability.
the construction of zero-energy solutions of Schrodinger equations with rational potentials may provide an alternative approach to the study of quantum integrable systems.
the construction of quasi-exactly-solvable potentials with zero-energy bound states is a natural consequence of their relation to exactly solvable ones.
